pathway.title: Petco Health & Wellness Company, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Leverage is falling for the right reasons but remains the main constraint. Net debt over reported EBITDA fell from 6.58x at fiscal 2024 to 3.90x at fiscal 2025 and 3.58x over the twelve months to August 1, 2026, because earnings recovered and free cash flow was kept rather than distributed, not because add-backs grew; on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA the ratio is 2.78x, but that rests on about USD 94 million of add-backs that cannot be tested against the lender's definition. Net debt and leverage after the February 2026 refinancing and the September 2026 prepayment are not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation E01; calculation E02

- Coverage is adequate on cash paid but only moderate on any steadier measure. EBITDA covered cash interest 3.25x over the last twelve months, yet cash interest ran USD 28.10 million below interest expense because of payment timing, so cover on interest expense is 2.55x and on the run-rate coupons of the new debt 2.70x; after rent, EBITDA plus rent covered rent plus cash interest only 1.36x in fiscal 2025. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation E05; calculation E06; calculation E07; calculation E08; calculation E10; calculation E11; calculation E12

- Cash generation is the strongest support, but part of it is timing. Free cash flow was USD 186.95 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 237.83 million over the last twelve months, equal to 16.12% of total debt; removing the interest timing gap leaves USD 209.73 million, still enough to take net debt to the issuer's 2x adjusted target in about 1.59 years at constant adjusted EBITDA. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation E04; calculation E09; calculation E21

- Liquidity and the maturity profile are the main protection. Liquidity of USD 781.1 million covers the USD 40.50 million of scheduled term loan payments to 2030 by 19.29x, and 97.30% of principal falls due in 2031, but the undrawn revolver matures in March 2029, ahead of the term debt, and the covenant terms that govern access to it are not supplied. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation E03; calculation E15; calculation E16

- The operating recovery rests on cost cuts, not growth. Selling, general and administrative expense fell USD 132.71 million in fiscal 2025 against a USD 155.0 million fall in net sales, and comparable sales turned from a 1.6% decline to a 0.6% gain in the first half of 2026, but net sales rose only 0.1% and the second quarter included a USD 6.8 million net tariff refund, without which the issuer puts second quarter adjusted EBITDA at USD 115.4 million. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation E18; calculation E27; calculation E28

- Rent makes the cost base rigid and earnings sensitive to sales. Operating lease cost was 1.30x reported EBITDA in fiscal 2025 and total lease cost was 9.1% of net sales, so a modest sales fall compresses margin unless costs fall with it; cost and capex flexibility is real but already used, since capital expenditure fell USD 98.50 million between fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2025 and is expected to rise to about USD 140 million in fiscal 2026. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation E14; calculation E19; calculation E30; EX-99.1_2026-09-02_woof-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2

- Financial policy is creditor-aligned, but control and structure limit what can be assumed. The company pays no dividends and has prepaid USD 245.25 million of term loan since fiscal 2023, yet the sponsors control about 65% of the votes, the borrower is a holding company with unnamed guarantors, and the lender's definition of EBITDA, the covenant levels and the ranking of the debt are not supplied. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation E24; calculation E32

- Interest cost is rising even as debt falls. The term loan's weighted average rate was 8.1% on August 1, 2026 against 7.3% on January 31, 2026, about 59.94% of principal is floating, and 100 bp on the floating term loan would cost USD 8.98 million a year before any hedge, whose terms are not supplied. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation E17; calculation E31

runs.text: The main strengths are recovering earnings and falling leverage, liquidity of USD 781.1 million with almost all principal due in 2031, repeat consumables and growing services at about two thirds of sales, a financial policy that has favoured creditors, and demonstrated cost and capital expenditure flexibility. The main weaknesses are leverage that is still elevated with thin cover after rent, flat sales in a shrinking footprint, a rent-heavy fixed cost base, earnings that lean on issuer add-backs and one-off items, and sponsor control with unnamed guarantors and unseen covenants. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation E03; calculation E12; calculation E15

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: On February 2, 2026, the day after fiscal 2025 closed, the company amended its First Lien Credit Agreement and issued USD 600.0 million of 8.25% senior secured notes due February 1, 2031. New term loans of USD 900.0 million, due February 2, 2031 and priced at Term SOFR plus 4.25%, together with the notes and cash on hand, repaid the USD 1,500.0 million term loan that was due in March 2028 and priced 100 bp lower. The refinancing removed the 2028 maturity. It cost USD 28.442 million in cash, of which about USD 20.7 million was capitalised, and it produced a USD 11.84 million loss on extinguishment and modification that includes a non-cash write-off. The new borrowings of USD 1,500.0 million equalled the principal repaid, so it raised no new money, and no sponsor equity is described. Basis: 10-Q_2026-08-01_woof-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8; 10-Q_2026-08-01_woof-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-K_2026-01-31_woof-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 100, 133; calculation D10

The notes may be redeemed at a make-whole price before February 1, 2028 and at prices set in the indenture afterwards, and a change of control may trigger redemption; the indenture restricts additional debt, distributions, asset sales, liens and affiliate transactions subject to exceptions that are not supplied. The asset-based revolver was undrawn at 2026-08-01 with USD 546.0 million of commitments maturing on March 29, 2029, after a March 2024 amendment extended most of it, and its first USD 35.0 million tranche matured on March 4, 2026. The credit agreements name covenants on debt, liens, fundamental changes, investments and restricted payments and, for the revolver, a fixed charge coverage ratio, and the company reports compliance at 2026-08-01; the levels are not supplied. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_woof-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 100; 10-K_2026-01-31_woof-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 131–133; 10-Q_2026-08-01_woof-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11

In September 2026, after the second quarter closed, the company prepaid USD 75.0 million of the term loan from cash on hand, applied to scheduled payments in order of date; this subsequent event is not in any period figure of this module and no new debt issue is recorded after February 2, 2026. Basis: 10-Q_2026-08-01_woof-20260801.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-09-02_woof-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation for Petco Health & Wellness Company, Inc. (issuer woof-1826470), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the normalised statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and coverage built from the six supplied filings and releases, with statements in USD thousands and the money tables in USD millions. No credit recommendation is made.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has fallen sharply but is still elevated: net debt is 3.58x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at August 1, 2026, against 6.58x at fiscal 2024, so creditors depend on the earnings recovery holding rather than on a thick cushion. On issuer-adjusted EBITDA the ratio is 2.78x, but that rests on about USD 94 million of add-backs, chiefly joint venture EBITDA and equity compensation, that cannot be tested against lender definitions.

fields.value: Liquidity is adequate at USD 781.1 million, and the February 2, 2026 refinancing moved the term loan and the secured notes out to February 2031, but cash interest paid is running below interest expense because of timing, so interest cover of 3.25x on reported EBITDA flatters. The USD 75.0 million prepayment in September 2026 is a subsequent event; no pro forma balance sheet is supplied, so pro forma net debt and leverage are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported leverage fell because earnings recovered and debt was repaid, not because add-backs grew. Net debt on balance-sheet carrying values went from USD 1,417.681 million at fiscal 2024 to USD 1,236.399 million at fiscal 2025 and USD 1,181.928 million at August 1, 2026, while reported EBITDA rose from USD 215.568 million to USD 317.143 million and USD 330.469 million on a last-twelve-months basis, taking net leverage from 6.58x to 3.90x to 3.58x. The fiscal 2025 gain came from a SG&A reduction of USD 132.7 million (2,184.639 against 2,317.351) on net sales that fell USD 155.0 million, and from a USD 95.25 million voluntary term loan repayment in the fourth quarter; the issuer links the SG&A decrease to lower payroll and consulting costs and improved actuarial results from employee benefits optimisation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 1.56x in fiscal 2024, 2.54x in fiscal 2025 and 3.25x over the last twelve months, but the last figure is flattered. Interest paid, net, in the 26 weeks to August 1, 2026 was USD 39.419 million against USD 62.441 million a year earlier, while interest expense was USD 65.34 million against USD 66.791 million, and the issuer attributes the stronger operating cash flow partly to the timing of interest and rent payments. The senior secured notes pay semiannually, so the timing of the coupon dates around the quarter end is not established.

fields.value: Liquidity at August 1, 2026 was USD 781.1 million, made up of USD 293.498 million of cash and USD 487.6 million of undrawn ABL availability after USD 58.4 million of letters of credit. The February 2, 2026 refinancing replaced the USD 1,500.0 million term loan, due March 2028, with a USD 900.0 million term loan and USD 600.0 million of 8.25% senior secured notes, both due in February 2031, at a loss on extinguishment and modification of USD 11.84 million and USD 28.442 million of cash refinancing costs and original issue discount. The undrawn ABL matures in March 2029, before the term debt, and the annual report says it must be repaid, refinanced or extended before that debt matures; no facility matures within twelve months of that date, and term loan amortisation is USD 9.0 million a year, so almost all principal falls due in 2031.

Neither has a pro forma balance sheet in the sources, so pro forma net debt and leverage are not established.

fields.value: The refinancing costs appear as three different figures for different purposes: a loss on extinguishment and modification of USD 11.84 million in the income statement, USD 28.442 million of refinancing costs and original issue discount paid in cash, and about USD 20.7 million of costs capitalised against the new debt (USD 1.4 million on the term loan, USD 9.0 million of original issue discount and USD 10.3 million on the notes). The cash figure serves net debt and liquidity, the expense figure serves earnings, and the capitalised figure explains the gap between principal and carrying value.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a creditor-neutral reading is control without creditor-side visibility. The sponsors hold the voting majority, hold registration rights that allow large sales, are exempted from the anti-takeover provisions, and have waived the corporate opportunity duty, while the refinancing priced the term loan 100 bp wider and the adjusted earnings measure includes a 50% share of a joint venture's EBITDA, 11.3% of the fiscal 2025 total, that is equity accounted rather than consolidated. A debt-funded distribution, a transfer of assets to a non-guarantor subsidiary, a sponsor sell-down that changes control, or fees to sponsors disclosed in the proxy statement would move the view toward higher risk; restricted-payment limits that prove tight in the executed documents, a continued run of voluntary prepayments and sustained positive comparable sales would move it the other way.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Petco Health & Wellness Company, Inc. (issuer woof-1826470), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the integrated business and financial credit view built on the six supplied filings and releases and the three earlier modules; no rating, legal-capacity, recovery, relative-value or sizing conclusion is drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Petco's credit is improving but still leveraged: cost cuts lifted reported earnings and cut net debt to 3.58x EBITDA, and liquidity of USD 781.1 million with maturities pushed to 2031 buys time, yet flat sales leave the recovery unproven.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation E01; calculation E03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Coverage is thinner than the headline suggests, with EBITDA covering interest expense 2.55x and EBITDA before rent covering rent plus cash interest 1.36x, and the documents that would show covenant room and ranking are not in the evidence. The primary downside is a sales relapse on a rent-heavy cost base, which the scenario below puts at 4.33x net leverage before any cost response.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation E07; calculation E12; calculation E22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage is falling for the right reasons but remains the main constraint. Net debt over reported EBITDA fell from 6.58x at fiscal 2024 to 3.90x at fiscal 2025 and 3.58x over the twelve months to August 1, 2026, because earnings recovered and free cash flow was kept rather than distributed, not because add-backs grew; on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA the ratio is 2.78x, but that rests on about USD 94 million of add-backs that cannot be tested against the lender's definition. Net debt and leverage after the February 2026 refinancing and the September 2026 prepayment are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation E01; calculation E02

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Coverage is adequate on cash paid but only moderate on any steadier measure. EBITDA covered cash interest 3.25x over the last twelve months, yet cash interest ran USD 28.10 million below interest expense because of payment timing, so cover on interest expense is 2.55x and on the run-rate coupons of the new debt 2.70x; after rent, EBITDA plus rent covered rent plus cash interest only 1.36x in fiscal 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation E05; calculation E06; calculation E07; calculation E08; calculation E10; calculation E11; calculation E12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash generation is the strongest support, but part of it is timing. Free cash flow was USD 186.95 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 237.83 million over the last twelve months, equal to 16.12% of total debt; removing the interest timing gap leaves USD 209.73 million, still enough to take net debt to the issuer's 2x adjusted target in about 1.59 years at constant adjusted EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation E04; calculation E09; calculation E21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity and the maturity profile are the main protection. Liquidity of USD 781.1 million covers the USD 40.50 million of scheduled term loan payments to 2030 by 19.29x, and 97.30% of principal falls due in 2031, but the undrawn revolver matures in March 2029, ahead of the term debt, and the covenant terms that govern access to it are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation E03; calculation E15; calculation E16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The operating recovery rests on cost cuts, not growth. Selling, general and administrative expense fell USD 132.71 million in fiscal 2025 against a USD 155.0 million fall in net sales, and comparable sales turned from a 1.6% decline to a 0.6% gain in the first half of 2026, but net sales rose only 0.1% and the second quarter included a USD 6.8 million net tariff refund, without which the issuer puts second quarter adjusted EBITDA at USD 115.4 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation E18; calculation E27; calculation E28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Rent makes the cost base rigid and earnings sensitive to sales. Operating lease cost was 1.30x reported EBITDA in fiscal 2025 and total lease cost was 9.1% of net sales, so a modest sales fall compresses margin unless costs fall with it; cost and capex flexibility is real but already used, since capital expenditure fell USD 98.50 million between fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2025 and is expected to rise to about USD 140 million in fiscal 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation E14; calculation E19; calculation E30; EX-99.1_2026-09-02_woof-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy is creditor-aligned, but control and structure limit what can be assumed. The company pays no dividends and has prepaid USD 245.25 million of term loan since fiscal 2023, yet the sponsors control about 65% of the votes, the borrower is a holding company with unnamed guarantors, and the lender's definition of EBITDA, the covenant levels and the ranking of the debt are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation E24; calculation E32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Interest cost is rising even as debt falls. The term loan's weighted average rate was 8.1% on August 1, 2026 against 7.3% on January 31, 2026, about 59.94% of principal is floating, and 100 bp on the floating term loan would cost USD 8.98 million a year before any hedge, whose terms are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation E17; calculation E31

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against the improving view is that trading has not yet recovered: net sales are flat, supplies and companion animals sales are still falling, the footprint is shrinking, and the profit gain came from cost cuts and a one-off refund while fixed rent absorbs any shortfall. If comparable sales turned negative again, the issuer's fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook of USD 415 million to USD 430 million proved too high, or the revolver could not be extended before 2029, the view would move toward weaker; two further quarters of positive comparable sales with cost savings holding, continued voluntary prepayments and adjusted net leverage reaching the issuer's 2x target would move it toward stronger.

fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-09-02_woof-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation E20; calculation E21; calculation E30

fields.value: - No peer, market-share or industry-growth data is supplied, so the judgements on scale, competitive advantage and diversification rest on the issuer's own account of its markets; this limits how firmly the Average ratings on those dimensions can be held, not the leverage or cover figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside scenario applies one illustrative sales decline at the reported gross profit rate with no cost response; it shows the direction and rough size of the pressure on leverage and cover, not a forecast of either.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The fixed charge style cover and lease-adjusted leverage are the analyst's own definitions built from reported lease cost and lease liabilities; they are not the lender's definitions and must not be read as covenant capacity.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The view stops at the second quarter 2026 report and release; the September 2026 prepayment is reflected only as a stated event, and trading since then is not known.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main strengths are recovering earnings and falling leverage, liquidity of USD 781.1 million with almost all principal due in 2031, repeat consumables and growing services at about two thirds of sales, a financial policy that has favoured creditors, and demonstrated cost and capital expenditure flexibility. The main weaknesses are leverage that is still elevated with thin cover after rent, flat sales in a shrinking footprint, a rent-heavy fixed cost base, earnings that lean on issuer add-backs and one-off items, and sponsor control with unnamed guarantors and unseen covenants.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation E03; calculation E12; calculation E15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Petco is a United States pet specialty retailer that sold USD 5,961.467 million in fiscal 2025, with consumables at 49.8% of net sales, supplies and companion animals at 33.0% and services and other, mainly veterinary care, grooming and training, at 17.2%, up from 16.3%. It sells through leased pet care centers, an e-commerce site and an app, and sales are substantially all on a cash basis, so receivable risk is small. The credit linkage is that roughly two thirds of sales are consumables and services that recur through the year, which supports cash-flow visibility and debt service, while the shrinking store base, with 16 net closures in fiscal 2025 and 15 to 20 more planned, means the visibility is of a smaller business each year. The 2016 sponsor acquisition, the 2021 listing and the February 2026 refinancing are the history that shapes the capital structure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-01-31_woof-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 92; calculation E25; calculation E33; EX-99.1_2026-09-02_woof-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two sponsors, CVC funds and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, control the company through Scooby Aggregator, LP, which holds about 65% of the votes, can designate a majority of directors and benefits from controlled-company exemptions, so there is no independent-majority check. The borrower and note issuer is itself a holding company with nominal net worth that operates through an indirect subsidiary, and the guarantors are not named, so structural priority cannot be established even though consolidated figures describe the group. The credit implication is that sponsor-friendly action is limited by the debt documents and not by the board, which the evidence has not let us read; conduct so far has been creditor-aligned, with no dividends, no repurchases and three voluntary prepayments totalling USD 245.25 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sales are partly recurring and partly discretionary, and the discretionary part is weakening. Consumables fell 2.5% in fiscal 2025 and were flat in the first half of 2026, supplies and companion animals fell 5.1% and then 2.3%, and services grew 2.6% and then 5.2%, so the mix is shifting toward services, which carry veterinary labour cost but differentiate the offer from online sellers. The issuer attributes the fiscal 2025 sales decline to lower transaction volume and a lower center count, and says competitors have cut prices and forced it to cut prices on some products, so pricing power is limited. No customer concentration is described and no vendor exceeds 10% of sales, so the credit risk is volume and price in a contested market, not concentration.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure but not against a repeat of fiscal 2025's sales decline without further cost action. Total lease cost was 9.1% of net sales and operating lease cost alone was 1.30x reported EBITDA, so rent is the largest fixed claim after debt service; selling, general and administrative expense is also largely labour and is exposed to wage inflation and veterinary shortages. Management cut that expense by USD 132.71 million in fiscal 2025 and lifted the gross profit rate from 38.0% to 38.7%, so the cost lever has worked once; the reported EBITDA margin rose from 3.52% in fiscal 2024 to 5.32% in fiscal 2025 and 5.54% over the last twelve months, but part of the first half 2026 gross margin gain is the tariff refund and normalised second quarter gross margin was about flat.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow conversion is solid and capital expenditure is flexible, but the last twelve months flatter it. Capital expenditure was USD 127.097 million in fiscal 2025, 2.1% of net sales, split between about USD 54.06 million for pet care centers, USD 53.572 million for digital and technology and USD 19.465 million for supply chain and other, and down from USD 225.598 million in fiscal 2023 on fewer new centers and hospitals; free cash flow of USD 186.953 million in fiscal 2025 was helped by a USD 63.119 million inventory reduction and the last twelve months by interest paid USD 28.10 million below expense. Operating leases run through operating cash flow, so EBITDA is already after rent, and the fixed charge style cover of 1.36x shows how little room rent and interest leave.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is the force that matters most. Specialty chains, independent stores, online retailers, supermarkets, warehouse clubs and mass merchants all sell the same consumables, some with more capital, and price cuts by competitors have forced Petco to reduce prices, which caps gross margin and makes comparable sales the key swing factor for leverage. New entrants are a moderate threat, mainly independent stores with distinctive offers and online sellers; substitutes are strong for products, because the same goods can be bought online or at a grocer, and weaker for services, where veterinary care, grooming and training anchor the visit. Buyer power is high because consumers can switch freely and discretionary spending has softened, while supplier power is moderate: the ten largest vendors supplied about 40% of sales, none above 10%, vendors may leave on 90 days' notice, but owned brands carry higher margins and vendor allowances reduce cost of sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two factors are material to credit and the others are supportive background. Tariffs are the political factor: the issuer sources from Asia, tariffs and fuel have raised costs before, and a USD 6.8 million net refund flattered the second quarter, so cost pass-through is uncertain and the refund is not a run-rate benefit. Economic conditions matter through softening discretionary spending, which hits supplies and companion animals, and through floating rates on about 59.94% of principal; pet humanization and premiumization and a steady pet population are social tailwinds that support consumables and services, and e-commerce is the technological force that raises price transparency.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position are Average: the business is large, but market share is not supplied and the footprint is shrinking. Competitive advantage is Average because services, owned brands and an omni-channel offer differentiate it from pure retailers while rivals cut prices. Diversification is Average: three product groups, services and several channels, but one segment and one country, and no customer concentration is described. Cost and capex flexibility is Average because savings were delivered in fiscal 2025 and capital expenditure was cut by USD 98.50 million over two years, yet rent is fixed. Margin stability is Weak, though improving, because reported EBITDA margin moved from 3.52% to 5.32% in a year while sales fell. Free cash flow stability is Weak on history, being negative in fiscal 2023 and USD 49.68 million in fiscal 2024 before USD 186.95 million in fiscal 2025, with timing items in the latest year. Ability to refinance is Average: the February 2026 refinancing extended maturities to 2031 at a higher cost, no ratings are supplied and the revolver must be extended by 2029. Liquidity is Strong at USD 781.1 million with minimal amortisation, subject to covenant terms not seen. Financial policy and governance is Average: conduct is creditor-aligned but control is concentrated and disclosure of covenants and guarantors is not available. The main supports are liquidity, cash generation and policy, the main constraints are leverage, rent and flat sales, the trend is improving, and the missing data are covenant levels, ranking, peer data and pro forma debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the issuer guides fiscal 2026 net sales flat to up 1.5%, adjusted EBITDA of USD 415 million to USD 430 million, net interest expense of about USD 122 million and capital expenditure of about USD 140 million; those figures imply second-half adjusted EBITDA of USD 195.45 million to USD 210.45 million against USD 204.86 million a year earlier, so the guide assumes flat earnings, not recovery, and any miss reaches leverage quickly. The coupon arithmetic of USD 122.22 million agrees with the interest guide, and the September prepayment saves about USD 6.1 million a year at the term loan rate. Reaching the 2x adjusted target needs USD 333.11 million less net debt at constant adjusted EBITDA, about 1.40 years of last twelve months free cash flow. Over three to five years the revolver must be extended before 2029 and the 2031 balloon refinanced; sector tailwinds are pet humanization and a steady pet population, headwinds are competition, softer discretionary spending, tariffs and wage costs, and company tailwinds are services growth and the membership relaunch against higher interest cost and the loss of the tariff refund.

fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-09-02_woof-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2026-01-31_woof-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation E10; calculation E20; calculation E21; calculation E23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside is a relapse in sales while the membership relaunch and store closures are still working through, on a base where rent is fixed. If net sales fell 2.5% from the last twelve months level, the same fall as in fiscal 2025, the gross profit lost at the fiscal 2025 rate of 38.7% would be about USD 57.72 million; with no cost response, reported EBITDA would fall to USD 272.75 million, net leverage would rise from 3.58x to 4.33x, EBITDA cover of interest expense would fall from 2.55x to 2.10x and cover of run-rate coupons from 2.70x to 2.23x. That is a deliberate upper bound for volume loss, as management cut USD 132.71 million of expense in fiscal 2025 and can cut capital expenditure, and resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, because liquidity of USD 781.1 million covers scheduled amortisation many times over and nothing falls due before the revolver in 2029; the financial transmission is to leverage, cover and covenant headroom, not to liquidity, and the observable triggers are comparable sales, the gross profit rate and the revolver extension.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Petco presents an adequate business profile supported by repeat consumables, growing services and a creditor-aligned financial policy, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 3.58x on reported EBITDA, thin cover after rent and flat sales. Cash-flow durability appears adequate, with free cash flow of USD 237.83 million over the last twelve months, of which USD 28.10 million is interest timing. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on comparable sales holding, the revolver being extended before 2029 and the 2031 balloon being addressed from a lower leverage base. The primary downside path is a sales relapse on the rent-heavy cost base. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, the lender's EBITDA definition, peer data and a pro forma balance sheet. A comparison with typical leveraged retail issuers is not established because no peer data is supplied. Top risk: a sales relapse on a rent-heavy cost base.
